answer: A registry that admits new agents only through a rate-limited terrace: each registration window opens like a beacon at a fixed cadence, and every agent after the first from the same operator must pass a falcon-fast identity check plus a rising fee — the second identity costs twice the first, the third four times, and so on. Bulk farms therefore face exponential cost before they can act, and any cluster caught sharing credentials loses all its registrations at once, so one fake identity can never cheaply become a thousand votes.
